messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 PAGE: Elevated 5xx/504s from inference-private-gw (eu-west-1a). Alerts: gateway-504-rate, nat-conntrack-saturation. Linking dashboards: https://metrics.internal/redwood/inference/gateway. Please ack and triage.

marie: acked. i'm on call, pulling up traces and logs now. can someone confirm scope (all tenants or private only)?

alex: seeing a big spike in 504s at the gateway layer. Preliminary: gateway -> nat gateway -> internet peering path. 504s correlate with a sharp jump in conntrack entries on the NAT box (and a lot of long-lived translations). not classic port depletion but sticky conntrack entries not being evicted after peering route churn.

devon: copying logs now. running quick probes on gw hosts.

devon: output from gw-03 (eu-west-1a):
```
# conntrack -L | head -n 5
ipv4     2 tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.10.3.45 dst=54.23.12.91 sport=34562 dport=443 src=54.23.12.91 dst=10.10.3.45 sport=443 dport=34562 [ASSURED]
...lots of entries with conntrack-age > 300000s...
```
looks like translations aged extremely high, many > 24h.

marie: that matches what i'm seeing on the metrics: conntrack table size jumped x6 in 18m and eviction rate dropped to near-zero. dashboard: https://metrics.internal/redwood/inference/nat/conntrack. also some kernel logs showing "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet".

alex: hypothesis: we had a peering route flap ~30m ago causing TCP flows to be re-routed across AZs while conntrack entries remained local to the previous NAT instance. when connections come back they create duplicates/stale entries and evict logic isn't keeping up. combined with an app traffic pattern (lots of keepalive-ish sessions), table got sticky.

sre-oncall: direct question to infra: can we do a staged conntrack flush on the NAT fleet? careful — that'll drop connections. we should do one AZ at a time and monitor.

devon: agreed. plan: 1) mark eu-west-1a as maintenance in the routing plane so new flows avoid gw-03; 2) run conntrack -F on gw-03; 3) monitor 5xx rates; 4) repeat per AZ if needed. i'll run step 1 now and coordinate with net team.

ops-bot: Runbook link: private-vpc-nat-conntrack-eviction (https://runbooks.internal/runbook/nat-conntrack-evict). Recommended: staggered flush, 30s wait, verify application telemetry.

support-lead: customer-impact snapshot: approx 12% of private VPC inference calls returned 502/504 in the last 20m. top impacted customers: AcmeAI (prod), Widgetly (staging). AcmeAI has an open P0 now. Please prepare an initial update for them: we are actively mitigating and will follow up with RCA.

marie: starting mitigation now on gw-03 (eu-west-1a). i'm toggling maintenance route and will run the conntrack flush in 30s. I will post exact commands.

marie: running:
```
# ip route replace ... (mark maintenance)
# ssh gw-03
# sudo conntrack -F
```

marie: executed conntrack -F on gw-03 at 3625001256. dropping ~180k stale entries. waiting for metrics to settle.

alex: telemetry update: 30s after flush, gateway 504s down ~60%, nat drop logs decreased, overall tail latency improving. good sign. still seeing elevated but trending down.

devon: pushed follow-up firewall tweak: expanded egress ephemeral range on gw security group to ensure peered hosts could reuse ports during the transition (SG egress allowed 1024-32767 earlier, bumped to 1024-61000). command: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc123 --protocol tcp --port 32768-61000 --cidr 10.0.0.0/8` -- double-checking with net team.

marie: after mitigation, errors are down to baseline for eu-west-1a. i'll hold for 15m then either rollback maintenance tag or proceed to eu-west-1b if metrics flare.

alex: root-cause hypothesis (tentative): peering route churn caused asymmetric forwarding; conntrack entries became stale/fragmented across NAT instances, causing table blow-up and evictions. security group ephemeral range constraint prevented smooth port reuse during reroutes. next steps: increase conntrack max on NAT hosts, add conntrack-aging tuning, schedule NAT session sharding and better cross-AZ affinity (longer term fix).

devon: created follow-up ticket: INF-7342 (post-incident: NAT session sharding + conntrack improvements). will schedule infra change window.

support-lead: drafting customer comms now. i'll post template shortly. please @me with any exact timelines.

marie: handing off to follow-up channel `#incidents-followup` for postmortem and remediation items. I'll also create a concise status note for customers. thanks all for fast coordination. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident SEV2 cleared (partial mitigation achieved). Please ensure postmortem is filed within 72h and link to ticket INF-7342.

sre-oncall: ending on-call thread. last check 3625001298 — metrics stable.
